text:
Suppose the vectors $x_{1}, x_{2}$ and $x_{3}$ are the 
solutions of the system of linear equations,
 Ax = b when the vector b on the right side is equal to $b_{1}, b_{2}$ and $b_{3}$ respectively. if

$x_{1}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]$, $x_{2}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]$, $x_{3}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$b_{1}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]$, $b_{2}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]$ and $b_{3}=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]$, 
then the determinant of A is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let A = $\left [\begin{array}{lll} a_{1} & a_{2} & a_{3} \\ a_{4} & a_{5} & a_{6} \\ a_{7} & a_{8} & a_{9} \end{array}\right ]$

For $Ax_{1} = b_{1}$ :

$\Rightarrow$ $\left [\begin{array}{lll} a_{1} & a_{2} & a_{3} \\ a_{4} & a_{5} & a_{6} \\ a_{7} & a_{8} & a_{9} \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $a_{1}+a_{2}+a_{3}=1$ ....(1)

$a_{4}+a_{5}+a_{6}=0$ ......(2)

$a_{7}+a_{8}+a_{9}=0$ .....(3)

For $Ax_{2} = b_{2}$ :

$\left [\begin{array}{lll} a_{1} & a_{2} & a_{3} \\ a_{4} & a_{5} & a_{6} \\ a_{7} & a_{8} & a_{9} \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $2a_{2}+a_{3}=0$ .....(4)

$2a_{5}+a_{6}=2$ ....(5)

$2a_{8}+a_{9}=0$ ....(6)

For $Ax_{3} = b_{3}$ :

$\left [\begin{array}{lll} a_{1} & a_{2} & a_{3} \\ a_{4} & a_{5} & a_{6} \\ a_{7} & a_{8} & a_{9} \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $a_{3}=0$

$a_{6}=0$

$a_{9}=2$

Putting value of $a_{3}$ in equation (4), we get

$a_{2}$ = 0

Putting value of $a_{6}$ in equation (5), we get

$a_{5}$ = 1

Putting value of $a_{9}$ in equation (6), we get

$a_{8}$ = -1

Putting value of $a_{2}$ and $a_{3}$ in equation (1), we get

$a_{1}$ = 1

Putting value of $a_{5}$ and $a_{6}$ in equation (2), we get

$a_{4}$ = -1

Putting value of $a_{8}$ and $a_{9}$ in equation (3), we get

$a_{7}$ = -1

$\therefore$ A = $\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$

So, |A| = 2(1) = 2
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text:
Let $f:(0,\infty )\to (0,\infty )$ be a differentiable function such that f(1) = e and 
$\lim _{t\to x}\frac{t^{2}f^{2}(x)-x^{2}f^{2}(t)}{t-x}=0$.  If f(x) = 1, then x is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{t\to x}\frac{t^{2}f^{2}(x)-x^{2}f^{2}(t)}{t-x}=0$

(Using L'Hospital's Rule)

$\Rightarrow \lim _{t\to x}\frac{2tf^{2}(x)-2x^{2}f(t).f^{'}(t)}{1}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $2xf^{2}(x) - 2x^{2}.f(x).f'(x) = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ 2xf(x){f(x) - xf'(x)} = 0 

[x $\neq$ 0, f(x) $\neq$ 0 as given 
function $f:(0,\infty )\to (0,\infty )$ only takes positive value as input and output]

$\Rightarrow f(x)=xf^{'}(x)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}=\frac{1}{x}$

Integrating w.r.t x, we get

$\Rightarrow lnf(x)=lnx+lnC$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=Cx$

$\because$ f(1) = e

$\Rightarrow C=e;sof(x)=ex$

When f(x) = 1 = ex

$\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{e}$

text: In a game two players A and B take turns in throwing a pair of fair dice starting with player A and total of scores on the two dice, in each throw is noted. A wins the game if he throws a total of 6 before B throws a total of 7 and B wins the game if he throws a total of 7 before A throws a total of six. The game stops as soon as either of the players wins. The probability of A winning the game is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Sum total 6 = {(1,5)(2,4)(3,3)(4,2)(5,1)}

$P(6)=\frac{5}{36}$

Sum total 7 = {(1,6)(2,5)(3,4)(4,3)(5,2)(6,1)}

$P(7)=\frac{6}{36}$  = $\frac{1}{6}$

Game ends and A wins if A throws 6 in $1^{st}$
throw or A don’t throw 6 in $1^{st}$ throw, B don’t
throw 7 in $1^{st}$ throw and then A throw 6 in his
2
$^{nd}$ chance and so on.

P(A) = A + $A–B–A$ + $A–B–A–B–A$

= $\frac{5}{36}+\left (\frac{31}{36}\right )\left (\frac{30}{36}\right )\left (\frac{5}{36}\right )+$ ..... $\infty$

= $\frac{\frac{5}{36}}{1-\left (\frac{31}{36}\right )\left (\frac{30}{36}\right )}$

= $\frac{5\times 36}{36\times 36-31\times 30}$

= $\frac{30}{61}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{π}{4}+\tan ^{-1}x, & x\in [-1,1] \\ \frac{1}{2}(x-1), & x>1 \\ \frac{1}{2}(-x-1), & x<-1 \end{array} \right.$

At x = 1

L.H.L = $\lim _{x\to 1^{-}}\left (\frac{π}{4}+\tan ^{-1}x\right )$ = $\frac{π}{4}+\frac{π}{4}$ = $\frac{π}{2}$

f(1) = $\frac{π}{4}+\tan ^{-1}x$ = $\frac{π}{4}+\frac{π}{4}$ = $\frac{π}{2}$

R.H.L = $\lim _{x\to 1^{+}}\left (\frac{1}{2}(x-1)\right )$ = 0

As L.H.L $\neq$ R.H.L so function is discontinuous $\Rightarrow$ non differentiable.

At x = -1

L.H.L = $\lim _{x\to -1^{-}}\left (\frac{1}{2}(-x-1)\right )$ = $\frac{1}{2}(-(-1)-1)$ = 0

f(-1) = $\frac{π}{4}+\tan ^{-1}(-1)$ = $\frac{π}{4}-\frac{π}{4}$ = 0

R.H.L = $\lim _{x\to -1^{+}}\left (\frac{π}{4}+\tan ^{-1}x\right )$ 

= $\frac{π}{4}+\tan ^{-1}(-1)$ = $\frac{π}{4}-\frac{π}{4}$ = 0

As L.H.L = f(-1) = R.H.L so function is continuous.

$f^{'}(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}, & x\in [-1,1] \\ \frac{1}{2}, & x>1 \\ -\frac{1}{2}, & x<-1 \end{array} \right.$

For differentiability at x = –1

L.H.D = $-\frac{1}{2}$

R.H.D. = $\frac{1}{2}$

So, non differentiable at x = –1

text:
Let $λ\neq 0$  be in R. If $α$ and $β$ are the roots of the 
equation, $x^{2} - x + 2λ$ = 0 and $α$ and $γ$ are the roots of 
the equation, $3x^{2}-10x+27λ=0$, then $\frac{βγ}{λ}$  is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α$ and $β$ are the roots of the 
equation $x^{2} - x + 2λ$ = 0 .....(1)

$\therefore$ $α+β=1,αβ=2λ$

$α$ and $γ$ are the roots of 
the equation, $3x^{2}-10x+27λ=0$ ......(2)

$\therefore$ $α+γ$ = $\frac{10}{3}$, $αγ$ = $\frac{27λ}{3}$ = 9$λ$

Multiplying equation (1) by 3 and subtracting form equation (2) we get

-7x + 21$λ$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ x = 3$λ$

$\therefore$ $α$ = 3$λ$

As $α$ is root of equation (1) so

$α^{2}$ - $α$ +  2$λ$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 9$λ^{2}$ - 3$λ$ +  2$λ$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = $\frac{1}{9}$

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = 3$\times$ $\frac{1}{9}$ = $\frac{1}{3}$

Also $αβ=2λ$ = $\frac{2}{9}$

$\Rightarrow$ $β$ = $\frac{2}{3}$

Also $αγ$  = 9$λ$ = 9$\times$ $\frac{1}{9}$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $γ$ = 3

$\therefore$ $\frac{βγ}{λ}$ = $\frac{\frac{2}{3}.3}{\frac{1}{9}}$ = 18
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text: Let $\cup _{i=1}^{50}X_{i}=\cup _{i=1}^{n}Y_{i}=T$  where each $X_{i}$ contains 10 elements and each $Y_{i}$ contains 5 elements. If each element of the set T is an element of exactly 20 of sets $X_{i}$’s and exactly 6 of sets $Y_{i}$’s, then n is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\cup _{i=1}^{50}X_{i}=$ $X_{1}, X_{2},....., X_{50} = 50$ sets. Given each sets having 10 elements.

So total elements = 50 $\times$ 10

$\cup _{i=1}^{n}Y_{i}=$ $Y_{1}, Y_{2},....., Y_{n} = n$ sets. Given each sets having 5 elements.

So total elements = 5 $\times$ n

Now each element of set T contains exactly 20 of sets $X_{i}$.

So number of effective elements in set T = $\frac{50\times 10}{20}$

Also each element of set T contains exactly 6 of sets $Y_{i}$.

So number of effective elements in set T = $\frac{5\times n}{6}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{50\times 10}{20}$ = $\frac{5\times n}{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ n = 30
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text:
Let {x} and [x] denote the fractional part of x and 
the greatest integer $\leq$ x respectively of a real
 number x. If $\int\limits _{0}^{n}\{x\}dx,\int\limits _{0}^{n}[x]dx$ and $10(n^{2} – n)$, 
$(n\in N,n>1)$  are three consecutive terms of a G.P., then n is equal $to_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{n}\{x\}dx=n\int\limits _{0}^{1}xdx=n\left (\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right )_{0}^{1}=\frac{n}{2}$

[As period of {x} = 1]

$\int\limits _{0}^{n}[x]dx=\int\limits _{0}^{1}0dx+\int\limits _{1}^{2}1dx+...+\int\limits _{n-1}^{n}(n-1)dx$

= 1 + 2 + 3 + ....+ (n - 1)

= $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$

As $\frac{n}{2}$, $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$, $10(n^{2} – n)$ are in GP.

$\therefore$ $\left [\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\right ]^{2}=\frac{n}{2}\times 10\left (n^{2}-n\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $n^{2}$
 = 21n

$\Rightarrow$ n = 21
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text: A test consists of 6 multiple choice questions, each having 4 alternative answers of which only one is correct. The number of ways, in which a candidate answers all six questions such that exactly four of the answers are correct, is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Select any 4 questions in $^{6}C_{4}$
 ways which are
correct.

Answering right option for each question is possible in 1 way.

So ways of choosing right option for 4 questions $= 1.1.1.1 = (1)^{4}$

Number of ways of choosing wrong option for each question = 3

So ways of choosing wrong option for 2 questions $= (3)^{2}$

$\therefore$ Required number of ways $= ^{6}C_{4}.(1)^{4}.(3)^{2} = 135$

text:
If $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$,  then the value of

$\left |\hat{i}\times \left (\vec{a}\times \hat{i}\right )\right |^{2}+\left |\hat{j}\times \left (\vec{a}\times \hat{j}\right )\right |^{2}+\left |\widehat{k}\times \left (\vec{a}\times \widehat{k}\right )\right |^{2}$ is equal $to____$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $\vec{a}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$

Now $\hat{i}\times \left (\vec{a}\times \hat{i}\right )=\left (\hat{i}.\hat{i}\right )\vec{a}-\left (\hat{i}.\vec{a}\right )\hat{i}$

= $y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$

Similarly $\hat{j}\times \left (\vec{a}\times \hat{j}\right )=x\hat{i}+z\widehat{k}$

$\widehat{k}\times \left (\vec{a}\times \widehat{k}\right )=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}$

Now $\left |y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}\right |^{2}+\left |x\hat{i}+z\widehat{k}\right |^{2}+\left |x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}\right |^{2}$

= $2(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2})$

Given $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ x = 2, y = 1, z = 2

= 2(4 + 1 + 4) = 18
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot
